core_sequence: ~10 m polymict crystalline impact breccia with shock features
~4.7 m graded polymict resurge breccia to sandstone/siltstone
facts.diagnostic_confirmation: shocked quartz PDFs in basement breccia below sediment infill; low shock pressures about 10-13 GPa

new_findings.effect_on_SR004: This is the closest confirmed shallow-marine impact analog found so far by diameter. It shows that a ~700 m marine impact may contain tens to >100 m of post-impact/slumped/resurge fill above diagnostic shocked basement. Therefore the negative coarse-fraction shock screen in only the upper 12.5 m of SR-004 is a weak anti-impact test.

facts.magnetic_character: central magnetic low/common simple-impact type with local complexity possible

new_findings.effect_on_SR004: A confirmed impact nearly the same diameter can have only an order-1 mGal gravity low. The absence of an obvious free-air low in SR-004 is therefore not strong evidence for a dense meteoritic body unless survey resolution, filtering and expected signal amplitude are quantified.

model.shape: finite cylindrical missing-sediment volume approximating a 600 m diameter, 40 m deep depression

new_findings.formula_note: finite-cylinder axial attraction integrated from z=155 to 195 m; used only as order-of-magnitude sanity check
new_findings.effect_on_SR004: The bathymetric gravity effect expected from the depression alone may be comparable to ordinary marine-gravity short-wavelength uncertainty/filtering scale. This weakens any inference that a missing low requires a dense object.

facts: simple and complex impact structures commonly show negative gravity anomalies due to fractured/brecciated low-density material
magnetic responses are variable and depend on target, fill, shock, heat and alteration
magnetic lows are common but magnetic pattern alone is not diagnostic
geophysical signatures can evaluate an impact hypothesis but confirmation ultimately rests on geologic/shock evidence
sources: review: Impact structures in Africa, PMC4802546

facts: methane seep diagenesis can either enhance or reduce sediment magnetization depending on authigenic mineral pathways
high magnetic susceptibility can result from authigenic iron sulphides such as greigite/pyrrhotite in seep environments
other seep systems show magnetic depletion where magnetite is converted to pyrite
therefore a magnetic anomaly above a seabed depression is not impact-specific
new_findings.effect_on_SR004: The positive magnetic signal reported over SR-004 is reclassified from weak impact support to AMBIGUOUS_GEOPHYSICS until co-registered mineralogy and source-depth modelling exist.

facts.location_context: western continental margin of India / outer shelf-slope off Karwar

sources: Chakraborty et al. 2014/related Natural Hazards author version
Pillay et al. 2016 citation and discussion
new_findings.effect_on_SR004: Deep, steep pockmarks are already documented on the same broad western Indian margin. SR-004 is much larger laterally but its wall steepness and depth are not by themselves outside fluid-escape morphology.

reclassification.smooth_rim_without_upturned_ridge: WEAK_EVIDENCE_ONLY; marine impacts may lose/erode rims
